chapterTag.category: AP Calc BC BC-3 — Parametric & Vectors

body.en: When a curve is traced by a parameter \( t \), motion in the plane is captured by component functions and their derivatives.

\( \dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} \). Speed is \( \sqrt{(dx/dt)^{2}+(dy/dt)^{2}} \), and arc length is \( \displaystyle\int\sqrt{(dx/dt)^{2}+(dy/dt)^{2}}\,dt \). A vector position \( \mathbf r(t)=\langle x(t),y(t)\rangle \) has velocity \( \mathbf r'(t) \).

figure.title: Parametric Trajectory and Tangent Vector: x = t², y = t³

caption.en: Parametric trajectory $x(t) = t^2, y(t) = t^3$ (Cartesian form $y = x^{3/2}$). At $t=1$, the particle is at $(1,1)$ with velocity vector $\vec{v}(1) = \langle 2, 3 \rangle$, yielding tangent line slope $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5$.

label.en: ⚠️ AP Exam Traps: Parametric & Vector Calculus

body.en:
• The Second Derivative Formula: The second derivative with respect to \( x \) is \( \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{\frac{d}{dt}\left[\frac{dy}{dx}\right]}{\frac{dx}{dt}} \). It is NEVER \( \frac{y''(t)}{x''(t)} \)! You must differentiate \( \frac{dy}{dx} \) with respect to \( t \) and then divide the entire result by \( \frac{dx}{dt} \).
  • Speed vs. Velocity Vector: Velocity is a vector with direction: \( \vec{v}(t) = \langle x'(t), y'(t) \rangle \). Speed is a scalar magnitude: \( \text{Speed} = \|\vec{v}(t)\| = \sqrt{(x'(t))^2 + (y'(t))^2} \). Always check whether a question asks for speed or velocity.
  • Total Distance vs. Displacement:
    • Total distance traveled is the integral of speed: \( \int_a^b \sqrt{(x'(t))^2 + (y'(t))^2}\,dt \).
    • Displacement is the vector net change: \( \langle x(b) - x(a), y(b) - y(a) \rangle \).
  • Particle at Rest: A particle is at rest if and only if both components are simultaneously zero: \( x'(t) = 0 \) and \( y'(t) = 0 \). If only \( x'(t) = 0 \), the curve has a vertical tangent; if only \( y'(t) = 0 \), the curve has a horizontal tangent.

Find the arc length of \(x=t^2,\;y=\tfrac{2}{3}t^3\) from \(t=0\) to \(t=1\).\[\frac{dx}{dt}=2t,\quad\frac{dy}{dt}=2t^2.\]\[L=\int_0^1\sqrt{4t^2+4t^4}\,dt=\int_0^1 2t\sqrt{1+t^2}\,dt=\left[\tfrac{2}{3}(1+t^2)^{3/2}\right]_0^1=\tfrac{2}{3}(2^{3/2}-1)=\tfrac{2(2\sqrt2-1)}{3}.\]

question.en: A particle moves with \(x(t)=\cos t,\;y(t)=\sin t\). Find the speed at \(t=\pi/4\) and the total distance travelled from \(t=0\) to \(t=\pi\).
A curve is given parametrically by \(x(t) = t^3 - 3t\) and \(y(t) = t^2\). Find \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\) at \(t = 2\).

solution.en: First compute derivatives: \(x'(t) = 3t^2 - 3\) and \(y'(t) = 2t\). The first derivative is \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2t}{3t^2 - 3}\). Next differentiate with respect to \(t\) using the quotient rule: \(\frac{d}{dt}\left[\frac{dy}{dx}\right] = \frac{(3t^2 - 3)(2) - (2t)(6t)}{(3t^2 - 3)^2} = \frac{6t^2 - 6 - 12t^2}{(3t^2 - 3)^2} = \frac{-6t^2 - 6}{(3t^2 - 3)^2}\). At \(t = 2\), \(3(2)^2 - 3 = 9\), so \(\frac{d}{dt}\left[\frac{dy}{dx}\right] = \frac{-6(4)-6}{9^2} = \frac{-30}{81} = -\frac{10}{27}\). Finally, \(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{-10/27}{x'(2)} = \frac{-10/27}{9} = -\frac{10}{243}\).
